title: Materiality: 96 of 101 orders are material under the illustrative project aggregation
description: With the illustrative test thresholds (single order 25,000,000 cents; 30-day window; project as the only grouping key) the materiality engine marks 96 of the 101 Builder Zero purchase orders material. That is a calibration issue with an illustrative key and window, not a default and not a finding about the engine.
linked_items: DEC-A1-8 (aggregation key and window); DEC-A1-1; golden materiality_summary
how_it_is_handled_here: Kept in the programme record. No threshold, key or window is chosen by the builder; the golden file records the observation, and later milestones use the policy as configuration.

title: Audit chain: a careful rewrite of the newest events cannot be detected by the chain alone
description: A hash chain detects edits that break a link. An attacker who recomputes the hashes of the last events leaves a chain that verifies. Detecting that needs an independent anchor of the chain head.
how_it_is_handled_here: Stated limit in the M2 contract suite; entry EDR-21 carries the full description. No change in M3.

title: Tenant isolation alone does not stop an authorised tenant user writing directly to a policy or decision record
description: The control functions check roles, but a session that holds only a tenant role could call the store directly and write a protected record kind. The port contract scopes by tenant and does not know roles.
how_it_is_handled_here: Stated limit in M2. M3 adds new kinds (recon_state, quarantine, entity_alias, entity_resolution, extracted_document, job) that need the same protection; they are named here for the Engine to decide under EDR-20, whose text is unchanged from M2.

title: The full M2 wrapper run was too slow for the auditor in one sitting
description: The auditor re-ran each M2 check separately but not the single wrapper that runs them all, which exceeded the auditor time limit.
how_it_is_handled_here: The M3 wrapper prints the time taken by each step and every step can be run on its own (RUN_COMMANDS.txt). The long mutation runs are separate commands, not part of the wrapper.
status: Handled in the package; for the auditor to confirm

title: The source name on a delivery is trusted
description: ingest_file receives a source name (for example accounting) and uses it to decide which authority rule applies. Nothing in this build checks that the person or connector delivering the file is registered for that source.
how_it_is_handled_here: Stated in the handoff register. Tests show the pipeline refuses tenant spoofing; they cannot show source spoofing is refused because that needs the Engine.

title: A job worker needs its own service identity to record a terminal failure
description: If the credentials that submitted a job are revoked or expire during retries, the tenant store refuses the dead-letter record. The reference runner keeps the failure in an unrecorded list and reports recorded false, so it is not lost silently, but a real worker needs an identity of its own to write it.
how_it_is_handled_here: Contract case JR-08 requires the failure to be reported; the identity question is in the EDR-04 decisions for Amir.

title: A whole file is written as one all-or-nothing batch
description: The pipeline writes a file as one atomic batch so a failed file leaves nothing behind. A real database may limit batch size or duration; splitting a file removes the all-or-nothing guarantee unless the receipt design is changed.
how_it_is_handled_here: This build limits a file to 100,000 rows and 5 MB by default (configuration, not a product decision).

title: The document extractor is a stand-in
description: The text reader handles the two Builder Zero quote documents. It exists to test the human-verification rule and the ambiguity handling. It is not an extraction product and was not run on any real PDF, scan or email.
how_it_is_handled_here: Extracted values are never authoritative until a person with the document_verifier role verifies them against the document hash.

title: Invoice-versus-order amount and price variance is not an ingestion check
description: Ingestion checks that an order exists and is consistent with the invoice link (PO_NOT_VISIBLE and the PO mismatch codes). Whether an invoice exceeds its order or a rate drifts is detection, and is left to M5 with thresholds from the product owner.
how_it_is_handled_here: No variance threshold exists in M3.

title: Identical purchase orders are held for a person before detection can use them (PS-17)
description: PO-0100 and PO-0101 are identical. Ingestion holds both as DUPLICATE_CANDIDATE and does not choose one. The M5 rule for surplus ordering will therefore see both as pending until a reviewer decides.
how_it_is_handled_here: Recorded so M5 handles pending orders explicitly rather than assuming both count.

title: Which missing optional values are tolerable is configuration, and the demonstration set is the builder choice
description: The default policy blocks use of any record with a missing optional value. Builder Zero needs a short tolerated list (for example GST amount on an invoice) so that most records are usable. That list is a demonstration choice, not a product decision.
how_it_is_handled_here: The list lives in demo_setup.DEMO_POLICY; a real list comes from the product owner and pilot builders. Material fields can never be tolerated.

title: A stored job result loses tenant-like keys
description: The tenant-scope guard removes tenant-like keys from anything written to the store, including a job result. The runner now returns the stored form, so a replay returns exactly what the first run returned.
how_it_is_handled_here: Behaviour is tested. Handlers should not return tenant-like keys.

title: Reissue detection is a naming pattern only
description: INV-0185 is shown as a reissue candidate of INV-0184 because of the invoice-number pattern and the credit link. That is lineage information only. It never changes a total; a person must decide.
how_it_is_handled_here: Stated in the lineage record itself.

title: The M3 project-filtered cost view skips conflict markers
description: The M3 invoice cost view, when given a project, reads each record's project field and a conflict marker has none, so a conflicted invoice would silently drop out of one project's figure. The unfiltered tenant total is correct and is unchanged.
how_it_is_handled_here: M3 is not changed. M4 attributes records with one rule shared by the gatherer and the calculations; a conflict marker whose versions name one project counts as held on that project, and one that names several is listed as unattributed on every project.
status: Handled in the package (M3 files unchanged)

title: The M4 tests found defects in the builder's own first drafts
description: While writing tests, five defects in the first drafts were found and corrected: retention events were not read when a calculation gathered its inputs; a set of security instruments that were all held showed zero instead of unknown; the percentage calculation quietly used forecast revenue for any unrecognised denominator; a negative retention balance, cost-to-complete, facility figure or project value was accepted; a figure that was not authoritative could carry no reason.
how_it_is_handled_here: Each has a test that fails on the earlier behaviour. The figure rule is now: a figure that is not authoritative must say why, and a parent names the component it is waiting on.

title: The financial intake repeats the M3 delivery loop
description: To leave M3 files unchanged, apg/fin/intake.py repeats the M3 file-ingestion loop for the new entities. Two copies can drift apart.
how_it_is_handled_here: Recommended after M4: one loop that takes the entity rules as an argument. Not done here because it would change delivered M3 files.

title: Cost scope is supplier invoices only
description: Labour, plant, accruals and overhead are not in any M4 cost figure. Builder Zero has timesheet and plant files but M4 does not ingest them, and what counts as cost is open decision CR-02 A5.
how_it_is_handled_here: Every cost figure carries a limit saying so. The policy field has one allowed value today.
status: Open - for the product owner (CR-02 A5)

title: No receivables data and no balance history
description: Without client invoices, certificates and receipts the overdue-receivables component always reports that it cannot be assessed. Without a history of retention balances only a forward carrying cost can be estimated.
linked_items: EDR-26; EDR-25; CR-02 A2; CR-02 A7
how_it_is_handled_here: A cash-adjusted margin whose policy lists the receivables component cannot be assessed, by design. The default demonstration policy lists only the retention carrying cost.
status: Open - handoff entries EDR-25 and EDR-26

title: A rejected row leaves no trace in a figure
description: A row refused at intake (for example an invoice with a blank amount) is never stored, so no figure can list it. It appears on the intake receipt only.
how_it_is_handled_here: A later data-health view (M9, M10) must show rejected rows next to the figures they would have changed. Until then a reader must check the receipts.

title: Calculation records are tamper-evident, not tamper-proof
description: Hashes detect a changed result, changed parameters or a changed pinned input. A writer who can delete a record, or who can write a different record under a new key, is not stopped by them.
how_it_is_handled_here: The new record kinds (fin_policy, retention_event, fin_forecast_slot, repro_record and the financial entities) need the kind-level write authorisation and the audit anchor already described in EDR-20 and EDR-21; those entries are unchanged.
status: Open - handoff entries EDR-20 and EDR-21

title: The gatherer lists every record of a kind
description: To pin a project's records the gatherer lists all records of each needed kind in the tenant and filters in memory. That is fine for Builder Zero and wrong at the size of a real builder.
how_it_is_handled_here: Described in EDR-24 with the read operations required.

title: The M3 wrapper and the 561-mutant run were too slow to reproduce in one sitting
description: The auditor could not reproduce run_m3_all.py or the full M3 mutation run within the execution limit and therefore holds them as builder-reported.
how_it_is_handled_here: M4 splits its checks into named groups that each run on their own (RUN_COMMANDS.txt), prints the time of each step, and runs each mutant in one interpreter (the M4 mutation run can be split by module with --only). The M3 runs are unchanged.
status: Handled in the package; for the auditor to confirm

title: The aggregation key list changes what the aggregation rule reports, and the demonstration departs from the Builder Zero file
description: test_thresholds.json lists the aggregation key as the project alone. With that key 96 of 101 orders count as material (F-01), so the rule would report almost everything. The demonstration policy therefore groups by project, supplier, material and cost code. This is the builder's illustrative choice and the open decision DEC-A1-8 is not made.
how_it_is_handled_here: The policy has no default for the key list; the demonstration says in its ORIGIN table which values come from the file and which are the builder's own. Splitting a chain of orders each inside the window of the next is not detected (OQ-A1-7).

title: Carry-forward from the M4 review: verification limits and two weakly justified mutation survivors
description: The auditor passed the golden, corpus, register and M3 regression checks (201 frozen files byte-identical) but did not reproduce the full M4 wrapper or the 672-mutant run, and holds those as builder-reported. Two M4 survivors (MG-CMP-004 and CO-BOL-013) are justified only by "no input found", which is weaker evidence than a proof of equivalence.
how_it_is_handled_here: M4 is kept as delivered and is not edited. The M5 mutation run splits by module (--only) so that any part can be reproduced alone, and the M5 equivalents each state the evidence. The two M4 survivors stay on this register.

title: Carry-forward from the M4 review: the financial figures are not a complete or authoritative construction ledger
description: Actual cost is supplier invoices only. Labour, plant, accruals and overhead are outside every M4 cost figure, and all validation so far is on synthetic data. The unresolved financial policies (revenue recognition, cost to complete, tax, commitment statuses, carrying cost, cash-adjusted margin) stay configuration decisions. EDR-24 scalability remains open.
how_it_is_handled_here: Every M5 amount that builds on an M4 figure says which figure it used and carries the same cost-scope limit. M5 does not treat any M4 figure as final.
status: Open - for the product owner (CR-02 A5 and others)

title: The M4 financial intake loop is now shared
description: M4 finding F-16 recorded that apg/fin/intake.py repeated the M3 delivery loop. In M5 the loop takes the entity rules as an argument (a specs parameter) and the detection intake calls it, so there is no third copy. This is the one M4 file changed in M5, so the M4 mutation run for that module has to be repeated.
how_it_is_handled_here: The regression against the delivered M4 package lists apg/fin/intake.py and tools/mut_runner.py as the changed files and requires every other M4 file to be byte-identical.
status: Handled in the package; for the auditor to confirm

title: The aggregation severity is the value of the orders, not a loss
description: A cluster of split orders is reported at the severity of the aggregate order value, which is value at stake. No loss has been shown. The amount is labelled as a record amount, not as an estimate of loss.
how_it_is_handled_here: The signal says so in its limits. Using a different basis would change the severity band of every aggregation finding.

title: Delay holding cost cannot be quantified
description: Overlapping delay events are reported with their overlap days, but the cost of holding the site is not estimated: there is no counterfactual and the critical path is not known.
how_it_is_handled_here: The signal is unquantified and states why. No amount is invented.
status: Open - needs a programme source and a decision on counterfactual

title: The comparable-quote rule relies on declared pairs
description: R07 compares a quote with a reference only where a person declared the pair comparable. The landed-cost adjustment and the comparability gate belong to M6; until then R07 cannot find a comparison nobody declared.
linked_items: Section 08; M6 (PS-14, PS-15, PS-16, PS-17, PS-23, PS-25)
how_it_is_handled_here: Planted scenarios PS-14, 15, 16, 17, 23 and 25 are M6 items and are not claimed here.

title: The M5 tests found defects in the builder's own first drafts
description: Three gaps were found while writing tests and are corrected: a signal was accepted although its identity or material-change digest did not match its content; a detection run for an unknown project returned an empty, clean-looking result; the contract suite did not catch a notifier that altered the content or delivered out of order until two faulty notifiers were added.
how_it_is_handled_here: Each has a test that fails on the earlier behaviour. An unknown project now raises PROJECT_UNKNOWN.

title: Finding permissions are by tenant role only
description: A person holding finding_reviewer in a tenant can act on every project's findings in it. There is no per-project or per-object permission and no check that a reviewer is independent of the project.
how_it_is_handled_here: Recorded as a limit. The Engine permission model decides how a role is scoped.
status: Open - handoff entries EDR-01 and EDR-12

title: Detection and the monitor read whole kinds in memory
description: The gatherer lists every record of a kind for the tenant and the monitor lists all findings. That is fine on Builder Zero and wrong at the size of a real builder.
how_it_is_handled_here: No new port is needed beyond EDR-24, but the finding list needs the same indexing and the same read point.

title: The new stored record kinds need write authorisation
description: det_policy, det_ingest, det_monitor_run and finding are written through the tenant-scoped store. Tamper evidence and kind-level write authorisation are as described in EDR-20 and EDR-21, which are unchanged.
how_it_is_handled_here: Listed so that Amir includes the four kinds when the kind-level rules are written.
status: Open - handoff entries EDR-20 and EDR-21

title: Plant, labour and compliance data have no real mapping
description: The M5 intake handles the Builder Zero timesheet, plant hire, compliance, defect, delay and work-output shapes. How a real builder exports these, and whether the hours are paid or worked, is not known.
how_it_is_handled_here: Templates are examples; a malformed material field is rejected at intake and a malformed non-material field is held.
status: Open - needs a pilot builder export

title: Out-of-scope planted scenarios and M3 items carried here
description: M3 findings F-09 (invoice-versus-order amount) and F-10 (identical purchase orders held before detection) were carried to M5. The first is handled by R03 for order totals; unit-price variance needs line data that invoices do not carry. The second is handled by D01, which lists held records instead of using them.
how_it_is_handled_here: The limits are stated in each signal.
status: Handled in the package; unit-price variance open

title: The M5 portfolio could print $0-$0 for exposure that is unquantified
description: The M5 demonstration prints "between $0.00 and $0.00" for an interpretation with two findings and none quantified. The findings were listed separately as unquantified, so nothing was calculated as zero, but the headline could read as no exposure.
how_it_is_handled_here: Corrected in M6: the portfolio now carries range_display and quantified_amount_available; with nothing quantified the headline reads "no quantified amount available ... this is not zero exposure". Four M5 code files, one M5 test file and the M5 demonstration output changed (F-46); new tests cover it.
status: Handled in the package; for the auditor to confirm

title: Carry-forward from the M5 review: split-order detection still depends on an unresolved grouping decision
description: The aggregation key changes the M5 result substantially; the demonstration uses project, supplier, material and cost code, while the Builder Zero threshold file groups by project alone. M6 does not change the key and adds no grouping of its own that is presented as a default.
how_it_is_handled_here: Retained as an open product-owner decision. M6's own grouping choices (demand matching, duplicate window, portfolio grouping) are logged as interpretations I-50 and I-53, not defaults.

title: Carry-forward from the M5 review: detection is not scalable or integrated
description: The M5 gatherer reads whole record types and filters in memory, and the monitor reads all findings. The M6 gatherer follows the same pattern for materials, demand, quotes, readings, dockets, orders and observations.
how_it_is_handled_here: Preserved as a prototype. Engine-backed, tenant-scoped, indexed reads, durable stores, scheduled sweeps and delivery to named recipients are engineering requirements for Amir, not documentation: EDR-24, EDR-27 and EDR-28 stay open.
status: Open - handoff entries EDR-24, EDR-27, EDR-28

title: A tenant-wide procurement run pins identifiers of orders in projects the caller is not authorised for
description: The tenant run reads every order of the tenant so that it can recognise the information boundary, and its pin list (the exact records it read, which makes it replayable) therefore names order identifiers of projects outside the authorised set. No signal names such a project or order and a test asserts that; the pins do.
how_it_is_handled_here: Documented and asserted in a test, not changed. Whether pins of unauthorised records may be stored or shown to the caller is an Engine permission decision (EDR-29).

title: Carry-forward from the M5 review: financial scope, synthetic validation and the unreproduced M5 results
description: Actual cost is supplier invoices only, so M6 reference prices are the last paid order rates, not a cost ledger. Every rule and limit has been tested on synthetic data only. The auditor could not complete the full M5 wrapper in their environment and did not rerun the 678-mutant run, so those stay builder-reported.
linked_items: F-24; F-25; CR-02 A2 to A13; EDR-24; M5 review
how_it_is_handled_here: Every M6 amount says which record it came from; the M6 mutation figures and test counts are the builder's own and are not independently reproduced. The M6 wrapper keeps the M5 steps as named groups so each can be run alone.
status: Open - for the auditor and the product owner

title: Defect A, found by the M6 tests: demand coverage ignored units
description: The first draft compared an order quantity with a demand quantity without checking that both were in the same unit, so 300 kg of orders could cover a demand of 100 tonne. Orders in a different unit are now not assessed.
how_it_is_handled_here: Coverage returns cannot_assess (UNIT_MISMATCH) and the over-order rule records that it could not assess; order units are never converted (I-50). A test fails on the earlier behaviour.

title: Defect B, found by the M6 tests: a cheaper partly comparable quote could be its own baseline
description: The comparability warning (MP02) took the cheapest comparable or partly comparable offer as the baseline, so a partly comparable quote could hide a cheaper not-comparable one: the warning stayed silent although a cheaper wrong-specification quote existed.
how_it_is_handled_here: The baseline is now the cheapest like-for-like offer and the wording says so. A test fails on the earlier behaviour.

title: The extractor and the market feed are test doubles
description: The extraction stand-in reads two Builder Zero text documents; no language model, PDF, scan or e-mail was involved. The market feed holds only series a test loads. No market-data provider is connected, named or assumed, and no licence has been confirmed.
how_it_is_handled_here: The contract suites define what any real implementation must do and 25 faulty implementations show the suites catch the intended faults. Which sources are licensed and how data is retrieved remain with Amir and the product owner.
status: Open - handoff entries EDR-08 and EDR-09

title: The M6 Builder Zero supplements are synthetic, and some signals come from random synthetic data
description: The quote readings, tiers, terms, landed-cost assumptions, import checks and specification requirements in mkt_data/ were written by the builder for tenant zero_one only (none for zero_two). The three portfolio rate-gap signals (MP10) come from random synthetic order rates; the copper gap is thousands of percent and means nothing. PS-25 is reported without an amount because no demand is left uncovered.
how_it_is_handled_here: The demonstration and the documents say so; the golden file records the signals as they are; none of these values is used as an expectation about any real price.
status: Handled in the package; no real data exists

title: A ranking built from one supplier's own offers can be definitive
description: The ranking needs at least two rankable offers, not two suppliers. Two quotes from one supplier for the same specification can therefore give a definitive ranking of that supplier's options. M6 adds an information note saying so ("not a comparison between suppliers") and does not change the gate.
how_it_is_handled_here: Left as a product-owner decision: whether a one-supplier ranking may be definitive, and whether the gate should demand two suppliers.

title: M5 files changed in M6 (baseline-changed) and the M5 checks they require
description: To register the procurement formulas and fix F-36, M6 changed: apg/det/detect.py (the registered procurement formula ids), apg/det/findings.py (accepts those ids), apg/det/relations.py (policy reference prefixes mkt_policy/ and mkt_spec/), apg/det/portfolio.py (display), tests/test_det_portfolio.py, tools/run_demo_m5.py and regression/DEMO_OUTPUT_M5.txt, plus the M5 and earlier register-check and regression tools that would otherwise fail on the extended tables. All other M5 files are byte-identical.
how_it_is_handled_here: The regression lists every changed file against its delivered M5 hash and requires the rest to be identical. The M5 tests and the M5 mutation run for the four changed code modules were repeated (see the M6 documents).
status: Handled in the package; for the auditor to confirm

title: RFC-01 conflicts with the programme numbering and overlaps reserved sections
description: RFC-01 calls its planned engine "M7", the programme table already has M7 "Recommendations", and the RFC capabilities overlap reserved Sections 19 to 24 and parts of locked Sections 06, 10 and 12.
linked_items: programme/RFC_REGISTER.csv; CR-09 P4 and P7; CR-01 A1
how_it_is_handled_here: Reported in the RFC record and left unresolved: the M7 row, CR-09 and the locked sections are not edited. M7 (either meaning) is not started.
status: Open - for the product owner and the blueprint author

title: Minor limits of the M6 rules
description: MP03 (decision due) pools offers by gate class only and not by qualification, so a stale comparable offer can set the decision date; a demand of zero quantity is accepted at intake but produces no purchase requirement; the supplier rule reports observations over a minimum sample and nothing below it; the larger-tier note says the total paid is "higher" when the totals are in fact equal (a test pins that it never says "lower"); an order rate at exactly 90 days is current and from 91 days stale, the same rule as a quote.
linked_items: apg/mkt/rules.py; apg/mkt/landed.py; corpus A15, E11, E12
how_it_is_handled_here: Each is covered by a test or corpus case so a change is noticed.
status: Handled in the package; for the product owner to confirm

title: The M6 corpus runs against the builder's reference pipeline, not a storage-neutral world
description: The M5 corpus could be run by Amir against the Engine's storage through a world interface. The M6 corpus (tests/corpus_mkt.py) builds its worlds with the builder's own test helpers.
how_it_is_handled_here: Recorded; porting it to a world interface is Engine-integration work for the handoff at M12.

title: Defect C, found by the mutation work: three or more identical orders never served as the last-paid reference
description: The orders reconciliation holds back as possible duplicates name each other in one comma-joined code. The M6 reading of that code kept the joined text as a single name (for example "PO-2,PO-3"), so with three or more identical orders the lookup found no order of that name and skipped the reference. With two identical orders it worked.
how_it_is_handled_here: Each candidate is now named separately, and a test with three identical orders pins the candidate lists and the limit text. A test fails on the earlier behaviour.

title: Defect D, found by the mutation work: an order rate in another unit was not rescaled, and a deposit above 100% could crash a scenario
description: A last-paid reference was shown per the order unit even when the specification register declares a conversion to the requirement unit, while a quote is rescaled; the same material could therefore carry two bases. Separately, a payment-term deposit above 10000 basis points reached the financing arithmetic with a negative balance and could raise an error.
how_it_is_handled_here: The order reference is rescaled with the declared factor exactly as a quote is, and says so; a deposit outside 0 to 10000 or not readable as a number is reported as an evidence gap and no deposit is assumed. Tests cover both. Order rates of zero or below, and orders with no unit, are held at intake and never reach the reference.

title: Defect E, found in the Engine #17 Phase 0 discovery: an action approval stayed in force after the finding's evidence changed
description: In M5 and M6 the approved action of a finding recorded who approved it and when, but not the finding version or the evidence it was approved against. When a later detection run changed the evidence (version 1 to version 2, a new state digest) the signal and the version were replaced, but the status stayed action_approved and the approval fields were not touched, so an approval given on the old figures still read as an approval of the new ones. A probe on the delivered M6 tree showed it: the finding was action_approved at version 1 and action_approved at version 2 with the same approver. APG does not carry out actions or move money, so this is a defect in the integrity of the record, not a loss. It was reported to the auditor in the Phase 0 report (gate E17-A23); on 2026-10-15 the auditor directed a labelled, separately versioned correction under change control.
how_it_is_handled_here: Corrected in the separately versioned release APG-M6.1; the delivered M5 and M6 archives and their hashes are unchanged. An approval now records the finding version and the evidence digest it names. A changed digest ends the approval (kept in the action's approval history), returns the finding to action_proposed with no new status, and needs a fresh approval by a person other than the proposer. Regression tests cover version 1 to version 2, unchanged evidence, replay, an older run, and reuse of the ended approval. The change record names the defect, the impact and the exact files changed. Builder-implemented and locally tested; no independent review has taken place.
status: Handled in the correction release; for the auditor to confirm

title: A proposal written against old evidence could still be approved after the evidence changed, also when the approver named no version
description: The independent audit of APG-M6.1 reproduced it: an action is proposed at finding version 1; a later detection run changes the evidence to version 2 while the finding is still action_proposed; a person other than the proposer approves without naming a version. In M6.1 that approval was accepted and bound to version 2 and the version-2 digest, although the proposal text and the case for it were written against the version-1 evidence. M6.1 recorded proposed_version and proposed_digest on the action but nothing compared them with the finding at approval, and the M6.1 tests did not cover the case. The builder reproduced it on the delivered M6.1 tree with the same digests and accepts that the tests were incomplete. The same gap existed after an approval had been ended by changed evidence (the old proposal could be approved again). The suggested identifier was F-53; this release is the change control it is recorded under.
linked_items: apg/det/findings.py; tests/test_det_proposal_binding.py; tests/test_det_approval_binding.py; tools/probe_stale_proposal.py; programme/CHANGE_RECORD_APG-M6.2.md; F-52; F-54; I-65 to I-70
how_it_is_handled_here: Corrected in the separately versioned release APG-M6.2; the delivered M5, M6 and M6.1 archives and their hashes are unchanged. An approval is now refused (STALE_PROPOSAL) unless the proposal was written against the finding's current version and evidence digest, whether or not the approver names a version; a stale proposal is marked stale by the run that changed the evidence and is sent back by a reviewer and proposed again against the current evidence (no new status or transition). The approval entry point approve_action fails closed without the version and digest the approver was shown. Tests were written first and seen to fail on M6.1. Builder-implemented and locally tested; no independent review has taken place. F-52 also stays open until independently verified.
status: Corrected in APG-M6.2 (builder-implemented); open until independently verified

title: The exact text and context of a replaced proposal and of an ended approval were not kept in the audit trail
description: In M6.1 a new action_proposed transition overwrote the action record and kept only the approval history. The proposal text, who proposed it and when, and the version and digest it was written against were lost when a proposal was replaced; the history event for a proposal or approval named neither the action text nor the versions; and an ended approval kept who approved and when but not the text that was approved or the approver's rationale. The auditor asked whether the immutable history must retain this and said it is distinct from the stale-proposal defect.
how_it_is_handled_here: Corrected in APG-M6.2 on the builder's reading that it must (I-69, retained for review). A replaced proposal is kept in full in action.proposal_history; the proposal and approval events carry the exact action text and the versions and digests; an ended approval keeps the text, the proposer, the proposal version and digest and the approval rationale. Nothing is deleted and earlier events are unchanged. Builder-implemented and locally tested; no independent review has taken place.
status: Corrected in APG-M6.2 (builder-implemented); open until independently verified
